scenarios.title: T4-H1 GET lists books ordered by id
scenarios.given: Books with ids 1, 2, 3 exist in memory with distinct titles.
scenarios.then: Response is 200 with JSON array of 3 books ordered by id 1, 2, 3.

scenarios.title: T4-H2 GET filters by title case-insensitively
scenarios.given: Books with id 1 (title 'Dune'), id 2 (title 'Brave New World'), id 3 (title '1984') exist.
scenarios.then: Response is 200 with JSON array containing only the book with title 'Dune'.

scenarios.title: T4-H3 GET uses q= search case-insensitively
scenarios.given: Books with id 1 (title 'Dune', author 'Frank Herbert'), id 2 (title 'Brave New World', author 'Asimov') exist.
scenarios.then: Response is 200 with JSON array containing only the book with author 'Frank Herbert'.

scenarios.title: T4-H4 GET combines multiple filters all must match
scenarios.given: Books with id 1 (title 'Dune', author 'Frank Herbert'), id 2 (title 'Dune 2', author 'Other'), id 3 (author 'Frank Herbert', title 'Other') exist.
scenarios.then: Response is 200 with JSON array containing only the book with id 1.

scenarios.title: T4-H5 GET filters by synopsis
scenarios.given: Books with id 1 (synopsis 'A vast empire'), id 2 (synopsis 'Dune rules') exist.
scenarios.then: Response is 200 with JSON array containing only the book with id 2.

scenarios.title: T4-U1 GET rejects unknown query parameter (S11)

logic: Extract all query parameters from the request URL using urllib.parse.urlparse and parse_qs.
Define the known query parameter set as {'id', 'title', 'author', 'isbn', 'synopsis', 'q'}.
Check every query parameter name against the known set; if any name is unknown, return HTTP 400 with JSON {'error': 'unknown query parameter'}.
Start with a copy of all books in the BookStore.
Apply field-level filters: for each known query parameter present in the request:
- 'q': keep books where the query value is a case-insensitive substring of title, author, isbn, or synopsis (OR across those fields).
- 'id': keep only books whose id exactly equals the given integer value.
- 'title', 'author', 'isbn', 'synopsis': keep books whose field value is a case-insensitive substring of the query value.
- If multiple parameters are provided, they must all match (in filter); no AND/OR confusion across different field params is ambiguous.
Sort the filtered books by id in ascending order.
Return HTTP 200 with the JSON list of filtered and sorted books.
On any missing or malformed input to the filtering logic, return appropriate errors (400 for invalid id type, etc.).
